title: epan: Add the ability to add conversation filter protocols.
description:
Convert our conversation protocols to a dynamic list and add
add_conversation_filter_protocol(). Use it in the Falco Bridge plugin to
add protocols with conversation filters.

notes.body: Would it make sense to use add_conversation_filter_protocol here as well? That way, we have only a single point adding to the list and future changes may be easier to implement. To avoid a forward declaration, I just would move the init function below
Done. The init function needs to be public so that we can call it in epan_init, which I forgot to do in my first pass.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6711/diffs?diff_id=374752434&start_sha=5fec212ae1952137107ce390e3159784dbf39334#24d9549f75b11be2b87d25203d62d1b7c63198ec_31_27)
Can we implement a function for querying, that a protocol had been already added? Could be useful in init methods and to avoid duplicate entries

Just thinking out loud here. If the add_conversation_filter_protocol does the check internally and just does not do anything if the entry had already been added, a second function is unnecessary. But someone has to do the check
This does not check, if the protocol already exists. It will work now, but if plugins may add as well, it could fail leading to unwanted consequences.
The function should fail silently if the protocol already had been added. That way an extra check is not necessary for initialization.

Something I'm wrestling with right now is what constitutes a "conversation" in Logwolf. The current code strongly assumes that you want to analyze byte streams identified by addresses and port tuples. Logs seem to lend themselves toward activity identified by interrogative pronoun tuples (who, what, and where). For example, it's useful to move between log entries that match a user, S3 bucket, or host (which might be identified by its instance or container ID instead of a hostname).

A similar thing occurred to me while working with industrial protocols. Although you could often force our conversations to be tricked into thinking there are addresses/ports, but in reality it is just a band-aid.

Moving the conversations to a generic identifier might be a right thing to do, but that would require quite a rework. For now, you could get away, with adopting a special address version, which accommodates your needs for log files?

I was thinking that it might be useful to have a separate "activity" API that would allow you to correlate field,value tuples, e.g. ((ct.user.name,"Lenny"), (ct.s3.bucket, "credit_card_dump")). The API could initially be a thin layer on top of the conversation API by hashing the tuple and using the "id" routines such as conversation_new_by_id. This would let you build conversation-style features based on activity tuples without making the conversation code needlessly convoluted.
